meta.unit: one (part, config, field) triple, field in sbox/ttable1/ttable
meta.scoring: Result cells are scored on key recovery, never on sigma. A sigma appears only where no recovery was run at that cell, and it is labelled. THE TABLE QUOTES THE CHEAPEST KNOWN BREAK. That is a choice between two legitimate questions -- what the originally documented attack needed, against what the best known attack needs -- and this table answers the second, because a trace count is a statement about what an attacker must spend and quoting 25 000 where 12 500 suffices understates it. The scorer of record is `tools/table_recover.py`: a margin-weighted union over all six pair sets, both last-round adjacencies tried and the winner kept. A cell whose figure was re-baselined names what it superseded. A score of n/16 implies a completion search of 2^(8*(16-n)) over the bytes it did not recover, so the one-pager does not write the term out; the full table does.
meta.trace_count_caveat: A trace count is meaningless without the table's runtime address, the line offset, the --line-shift and the adjacency. Those live in the per-config 'src' and 'notes' fields and in the dossiers.
meta.paper_one_page_cmd: python tools/cross_part_table.py --format latex --columns onepage --terse --no-part-row --configs baseline --part-geometry notes --exclude rp2040,rp2350,stm32f415 --latex-env xtabular --latex-wrapper strip --out research/reference/crosspart.tex

repro.why: results/g4_ctguard/g4ct_codepad.npz is the CODEPAD sweep behind research/targets/stm32g474_latency0.md §4f: rigs/fw_g4_ctguard's own aes_sbox_encrypt with the tables in flash (R 0), four code pads x three FLASH_ACR words, 20 000 traces per cell, one array per cell named cy_p<pad>_<acr>. All four 0x000 cells (cy_p0_000, cy_p4_000, cy_p8_000, cy_p12_000) are ONE distinct cycle count, 5 139, sd 0.0000 over 20 000 random plaintexts -- 'flat -- 1 value in 20 000, at all four code offsets' exactly, 80 000 traces in total, and cy_p0_000 is the one named here. The positive control is in the same file and the same session: the 0x001 cells (LATENCY 1, DCEN 0) give 22 to 26 distinct values and the FULL KEY with a 0/16 wrong-key control -- the file's own record says 16/16 at 20 000 traces, and re-scored at the derived geometry cy_p0_001 is 10/16 at 2 500 and 16/16 from 5 000 -- so the rig, the placement and the scorer were all working and the flat reading is the cipher's. A second capture agrees at the whole-ACR level: g4ct_map.npz's cy_flash_000 row is also 1 distinct value at 5 139 with sd 0.0000, against an SRAM twin cy_ram_000 at 1 distinct value on the same build.  ONE CAVEAT THE DOSSIER MAKES ITSELF, worth carrying into the table: 'at all four code offsets' is not what CODEPAD 0/4/8/12 tests. gcc aligns each function to 4 bytes, so those four pads put aes_sbox_encrypt at offsets 4, 0, 4, 0 modulo the 8-byte flash read word -- two alignments twice each, which is the trap stm32l152.md §4.6 documents. Offsets 2 and 6 need a source-level 2-byte step and research/targets/stm32g474_arb_probe.md §4.2 supplies them: one distinct value at all four offsets, 0/16 each, with a 16/16 LATENCY 1 control each. So the claim holds, on two files rather than this one.
repro.loader_args_why: the CODEPAD sweep, same campaign and same shape as g4ct_map.npz. Its cells are flat, so only the distinct count is read, but the arguments are here so a block on one of them does not need a second lookup.

repro.function: aes_sbox_encrypt -- rigs/fw_g4_ctguard, the 256 B byte S-box, tables in flash
repro.line_off_derivation: DERIVED, not swept: line_off 0 and line_shift 3. The G474's flash read word is 8 bytes and every build's final round reads the 256 B byte S-box, so entries are one byte -- the same derivation the covered T-table blocks on this part use from SBOX 0x08001f00 mod 8 = 0 in rigs/fw_g4. For rigs/fw_g4_ctguard the base is 8-aligned under both link scripts: link_pad.ld puts SBOX at 0x08000770 (stated in stm32g474_latency0.md §4f) and link.ld puts aes.o's .rodata at 0x08002df0 per rigs/fw_g4_ctguard/fw.map, so the offset is 0 either way and does not depend on which image this capture ran. For rigs/fw_g4_align at SBOX_OFF = 0 it is 0 by construction: tables.h pads with a 32-byte-aligned aestab_pad[32 + SBOX_OFF] so SBOX lands at exactly SBOX_OFF mod 32, read out of the source rather than off a .map. The archived scores agree -- ctguard2_g4.py's recover() sweeps line_shift (3, 4, 5) at line_off 0 and records shift 3 in every leaking cell.
repro.why: THE FIGURE CURRENTLY IN THIS CELL IS A MEASUREMENT OF A DIFFERENT ROW, and this block replaces it with one at this row's own register word. '12-15/16 @ 20 000' is the ACR 0x00040304 column of research/targets/stm32g474_art_geometry.md's alignment table (15/16 at S-box offsets 0, 8 and 16, 12/16 at 4 and 28, sigma 8.8) -- LATENCY 4, which is config index 5's word, not LATENCY 1. results/g4_ctguard/g4ct_map.npz sweeps the whole ACR space on the byte S-box, 20 000 traces per cell, and its cy_flash_301 IS this row: FLASH_ACR 0x301, 18 distinct values, sd 2.2000, mean 5 295.04, against an SRAM twin cy_ram_301 at 2 distinct values and sd 0.1202 scoring 0/16, and a 0/16 wrong-key control. Re-scored at the derived geometry it is 4/16 at 2 500, 15/16 at 5 000 and 16/16 from 10 000 -- the FULL KEY, where the cell claims 12-15 bytes; the campaign's own record in the file agrees (bytes 16, shift 3, wrongkey 0). line_off 0 is the argmax at the rung where it means something: at 5 000 it gives 15/16 and the next best offset gives 11/16, while by 10 000 offsets 6 and 7 reach 16/16 as well -- a strong channel blurring the row boundary, so read the offset off the 5 000 rung and not off the threshold. ct_adjacent true returns 0/16 at every rung and every offset, the clean null a wrong adjacency gives. g4ct_map.npz is a 70-cell file but it stores FULL per-trace arrays rather than aggregates, so the matrix-capture rule does not confine it to a flat verdict; `observable` names the cell. SCHEMA NOTE, COMMON TO EVERY BYTE-S-BOX CAPTURE ON THIS PART: none of them carries ciphertexts, and g4ct_map.npz / g4ct_codepad.npz / g4_align_sweep.npz carry no key and NO SEED either -- the seed is a module constant (SEED = 0xC0FFEE in results/g4_ctguard/ctguard2_g4.py, a --seed default in results/stm32g474/g4_align_recover.py), which is the gap research/targets/stm32l152.md §4.1 notes about this part's deep run. So flashattack.archive.load cannot read them: it resolves a timing column only through cyc/cyc_cycles/cycles/timing and then requires a ct array. They are re-scored here by regenerating the plaintexts with flashattack.transport.gen_pts(0xC0FFEE, n) -- identical to both scripts' own prng_plaintexts, the device xorshift32 mirror -- and the ciphertexts from flashattack.aesref against fw_g4_ctguard / fw_g4_align's compiled-in key 2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c. A recovery succeeding at all is what confirms the seed. repro_triage.py validate cannot replay these blocks until archive.load grows a seed + known-key path; the covered T-table blocks on this part are unaffected, because g4_cell_capture.py writes cyc + device-reported ct.
repro.loader_args_why: the FLASH_ACR x code-offset map: one cycle array per cell, named cy_flash_<acr>. Neither the key nor the seed is a field; both were constants in the capture script.

repro.why: HOW THE CLAIM WAS ESTABLISHED, read off the file and not off the prose: results/l475/matrix.json is the 90-cell screen, n = 2048 random plaintexts per cell from seed 0xC0FFEE with jitter_n = 150 fixed-plaintext repeats beside it. Its five rows with tab = ram and prften = icen = dcen = false -- labels ws0+none through ws4+none, vos = 1 -- all read distinct = 1, chan_sd = 0.000, lo = hi, jitter = 0.000 and jitter_distinct = 1 for this implementation, with the table at 0x200000e0. I checked all five wait states, not one. The mean RISES across them, 1750 cycles at LATENCY 0 to 3755 at LATENCY 4, which is the configuration's own name working: the code is left in flash and pays the wait states, while the table it indexes is not. That is the table's 'flat -- 1 distinct value, ART off, every wait state', exactly as scoped, and stm32l475.md section 4's control table is the same numbers. There is nothing to recover from one distinct cycle count, which is why this is flat and not a 0/16. NOTE THE FIELD NAME: matrix.json calls the 4-table `ttable4` and the compact 1-table `ttable1`, so the one-page table's `ttable` column is matrix.json's `ttable4` and the firmware's aes_ttable_encrypt. Reading the columns across in order is how this gets filed one implementation out. WHAT THIS IS NOT. (a) It is NOT a claim about the RAM rows with the ART ON. The same file's ws4+PRFT+IC+DC ram row reads 2 distinct values for both T-tables (chan_sd 0.133 for ttable1, 2.519 for ttable4) -- but under fixed-plaintext jitters of 9.961 and 9.308, so those rows sit on the platform floor rather than carrying a channel, which is the control statement in the form _PROCEDURE.md section 4 asks for and a different statement from distinct == 1. The covered sbox cell on this configuration is backed by a deep capture at ACR 0x504, i.e. ART on. (b) IT IS 2 048 TRACES, which is the weak part of it and has to be quoted with the number. The byte S-box twin at this configuration has a 25 000-trace per-trace capture behind it (l475_sbox_ram_acr504_vos1_25000.npz, distinct 2, sd 0.063, 0/16 at margin exactly 0.000); neither T-table has one, and no T-table RAM .npz exists on this part. Section 8 names the precedent that makes this matter: the K21's screen-flat cell gave up eight bytes at 100 000 traces, and on this very part section 4b has two flash cells that read one distinct value at 2 048 traces at -O2 and are plainly not constant time at -O3. WHAT MAKES IT SAFE TO CALL FLAT ANYWAY: the -O3 twin exists and agrees. results/l475/matrix_O3.json, the same 90 cells rebuilt at OPT=3 with SBOX at 0x08005d00, has distinct = 1 for both T-tables in every ART-off ram row; I checked all of them and none is non-flat. cells.claim: n/s
cells.note: 'n/s' is not a result. Nothing was scored in this column at this configuration -- and the figure that belongs in it is the one currently rendered under `ttable` (cell B, 60 000 traces). THE WHOLE ROW IS RECOMMENDED FOR REMOVAL FROM THE RESULT COLUMNS, on three grounds that are independent of each other and each of which alone stops this part being read the way every other row is read. (1) WRONG IMPLEMENTATION AXIS. The firmware is ChipWhisperer's own simpleserial-aes with its vendored tiny-AES128-C, which is a BYTE S-BOX cipher: it has no T-table of any size. So the three figures the table carries are an `sbox` datum sitting in the `ttable` column while `sbox` and `ttable1` read 'n/s', and there is no build on this target that could ever fill the two T-table columns -- filling them would mean replacing CW's stock firmware, which is the one thing the part is in the table to characterise (research/targets/stm32f415.md's headline is that the STOCK build is the constant-time control). Everywhere else the three columns mean this project's own aes.c at three footprints, which is what makes them comparable across parts. (2) WRONG PAIR MODEL FOR TWO OF THE THREE CELLS. The dossier says so itself, in the section on the 12/16 plateau: tiny-AES pairs S-box reads within a state ROW with only three pairs per row, which 'is neither of the two adjacencies recover_k10() offers', and col_attack() taking the two ciphertext indices directly 'is the right entry point'. A repro block records (pairsets, ct_adjacent, line_shift, line_off) and nothing else, so it cannot express that read order. Measured here: cap_E_50k tops out at 6/16 over ALL SIXTEEN line offsets in both adjacencies at line_shift 4, and its ladder is FLAT -- 2/16 at 4 000, 4/16 at 12 500, 4/16 at 25 000, 4/16 at 50 000 -- which is the dossier's own diagnostic for a wrong model, against the 16/16 at 4 000 that col_attack verifies. (3) WRONG OBSERVABLE LABEL. The timing is scope.adc.trig_count on a ChipWhisperer-Husky, not the victim's own cycle counter, and it is stored under the array name `cyc`, so archive.load picks it up silently as a cycle count. Per the contract's second-observables rule `observable` would have to say trig_count -- and naming it that makes load raise, while naming it `cyc` is a false label. Add the geometry caveat on top: line_shift 4 rests on the F429's 16-byte row, which research/targets/stm32f415.md §3 and §8 say was NOT measured on this die, and DATASHEETS.md §A deliberately has no row for the part for that reason. None of this touches the part's findings, which stand in its dossier and in the ledger; it is an argument about one table's result columns. If the row is kept instead, the minimum honest change is to move the three figures into `sbox` and record the observable, and the artifacts are handed over per cell above.

cells.claim: flat -- 1 value in 150 000

repro.why: The capture holds the claim directly. stm32l552.md section 7a is the 15-cell cost surface -- ICACHE mode against LATENCY, TABLEPAD 0, tables in flash, batched Q 10 with a warm-up before each timed call -- and its ICACHE-off / LATENCY-0 row reads mean 5049.0, std 0.00, ONE distinct value, 0/8 recovered at every rung from 5 000 to 150 000. Re-read 2026-10-20 off the file: the cyc_off_0 array is 150 000 long and np.unique gives exactly 1, which is the table's 'flat -- 1 value in 150 000' with its n attached, as the contract's distinct-count gotcha asks. Section 7b is why it is a real zero and not a quiet instrument: the four cache-off captures share a PRNG seed, (cycles - min) / LATENCY is bit-identical across LATENCY 2, 4, 8 and 15 for 100.0000 % of 150 000 traces, so cycles = base(LATENCY) + LATENCY * M(input) with M a pure function of the input. At LATENCY 0 the miss is free, M is multiplied by nothing, and the latch -- which section 2c shows no register on this part can switch off -- is worth zero. The capture's own 1-way and 2-way columns are the same single value at every LATENCY, because at TABLEPAD 0 the table never shares a set with the cipher's code. No line_shift applies to this cell and none was used: with one distinct cycle count there is no collision to group, which is the contract's point that a flat cell has nothing to recover and a screen on one is not evidence of anything. TWO THINGS TO KNOW ABOUT THIS ARTIFACT. The observable is cyc_off_0, not cyc, because the file is a 15-cell surface with one cycle vector per cell. And repro_triage.py validate CANNOT load it: l5_surface.npz has no ciphertext column, so archive.load raises after resolving the observable, and this block will show as ERROR in a validate run. Nothing needs loading to support a constancy claim -- repro_merge.py's own docstring says it does not check that a flat verdict's capture is the one the claim was made from, and the artifact here is the capture plus its distinct count -- but the ERROR row is expected rather than a regression. The scope limit worth keeping with the row: section 7c makes LATENCY 0 an absolute mitigation only for an attacker with an exact cycle counter, since signal and noise scale together on this bench; for a remote attacker against a fixed noise floor the 1/LATENCY-squared law reasserts itself and that case was not measured. And LATENCY 0 is only in spec at low clock -- this board is HSI16 at 16 MHz, an L552 at 110 MHz needs 5 wait states and cannot buy the immunity back.

cells.claim: flat

repro.why: DISTINCT IS 2, NOT 1, AND IT IS READ OFF THE CAPTURE: 9998 cycles on 399 966 traces and 9999 on 34, sd 0.00922, n = 400 000, with the capture's own fields reading fcache 0, flwt 2, mhz 120.0, ram 0, selftest 0x1f. The flat claim is not that the counter never moves but that there is no data-side reuse left to be data-dependent about, and the mechanism measurement is what carries it: s5d3.md section 3b alternates two addresses and finds that with FCACHEEN clear, RE-READING THE SAME BYTE costs the full miss price -- 2.000 cycles at every gap from 0 to 4096, flat -- so there is no latch surviving behind the register, which is the RA2A1's result reproduced on a Cortex-M4 through a different wait-state register and is why `turn the accelerator off` is a complete fix here and is not one on the F429, G474, L552 or nRF52840. The recovery was run rather than inferred (section 5e): 0/8 at 25 000 / 100 000 / 400 000, every pair set, both adjacencies, max margin 0.000 against 2.015 for the positive control on the same path and the same part. The 34 outliers are section 5f -- same rate in the tables-in-RAM rows, scattered in time, and the FCACHEEN = 0 four-table capture has zero of them in 400 000. Corroborated at 2 048 traces by the matrix cell sbox / ram 0 / 120 MHz / flwt 2 / fc 0 in s5d3_matrix_bl_o2.npz, which is distinct = 1 at 9998, i.e. the 34 outliers are below that capture's resolution.

WHAT THIS CELL DOES NOT HAVE, and the other two fields in this row do: a deep capture. n is 2 048 here against 400 000 for the S-box and the four-table, and the dossier's own section 4b is the warning against reading a null off 2 048 traces -- the K21 read one distinct value at 2 048 and gave up 8 key bytes at 100 000. What makes flat the right verdict anyway is that the claim rests on a mechanism measurement rather than on this statistic: section 3b shows no data-side reuse of any kind with the bit clear, not even re-reading the same byte, so there is nothing left for any implementation to be data-dependent about, and the two implementations that WERE deep-captured at this configuration came back 0/8 at 400 000 with margin 0.000. A 400 000-trace capture of the compact build at FCACHEEN = 0 would close the gap and does not exist; it is cheap and is worth queuing with the FLWT-0 recapture this fragment files for the same field. Note the neighbouring `ttw_alt` cell at the same registers is distinct = 2 (sd 0.0221, one trace in 2 048), which is this platform's jitter floor and appears in tables-in-RAM rows too; `ttw` itself has none.

This is the configuration the table's row names -- the shipped registers with the tables moved, which on this part is also the FASTEST placement (4907 cycles against 5247 in flash, 0.82-0.94x across the implementations, section 6). The breadth is what carries this cell rather than the depth: the same capture holds 60 tables-in-RAM cells across five implementations x FCACHEEN x FLWT x clock, and 56 of them are distinct = 1 with sd exactly 0.00000. All four are at 30 MHz (ttw flwt 0 fc 1, sbox_alt flwt 0 fc 0, sbox flwt 1 fc 1, ttw_alt flwt 1 fc 0) and NONE is in this row; section 4a describes the same one-trace event as the platform's jitter floor and notes it appears at the same rate in RAM rows as in closed flash rows, so the prose overstates `every` by four cells and the three cells this row renders are not among them.

Section 6c is explicit that this image's table is at 0x2BB4 and that the line_off 0 which sections 5, 6a and the old section 7 used belongs to the other build family, at 0x6D00.
